ideas.risks: A hidden intermediate-horizon constraint or endpoint convention could force an extra term; strict-crossing implementation may need a separate eta-loss lemma.
ideas.summary: Audit the solver's claimed formula for the two-level prefix h^M,0^N,l,0^L,h: D_n = [l(M+N)-h(M-1)_+ ]_+ (1-l/h). Check M=0, M=1, N=0, L=0, all post-low intermediate horizons, and the quote-at-low-time convention. If correct, promote it as the resolved post-low single-drought lemma.
ideas.title: Verify Post-Low Drought Formula
ideas.why_promising: It resolves the iteration-15 target and gives the cleanest local regression test for any two-level debt recursion.

ideas.risks: Earlier low horizons may not be dominated by the final low; capacity constraints on where low-mass can be placed may make the LP more complex than the solver's sketch suggests.
ideas.summary: Generalize to one high-free episode with several low prices: h^M,0^{N_0},l,0^{N_1},l,...,0^{N_r},l,0^L,h. Formulate the exact LP with cumulative low-horizon surplus constraints S_j - l P_j and final high debt (h-l)P_total. Determine whether the last low alone binds or whether early lows create additional front-loading constraints.
ideas.title: Multi-Low Single-Drought LP
ideas.why_promising: This is the smallest nontrivial test of the proposed resolved-surplus/debt picture.

ideas.risks: Small finite examples may mislead, and numerical LP output will still need exact rational or symbolic proof before promotion.
ideas.summary: Implement the formal left-limit finite-prefix LP for two-level paths and enumerate short paths over {0,l,h}, plus parametric repeated diluted droughts. Extract primal marginals and dual supports; compare D_n against the solver formula, the stable-high gap Q_T, and candidate debt recursions.
ideas.title: Exact Two-Level LP Experiments
ideas.why_promising: The gluing problem has repeatedly defeated intuition; exact finite-prefix computations can quickly falsify proposed recursions or reveal stable invariants.

ideas.risks: Local drought costs may not add because the same quote marginals serve overlapping future horizons; old high history can damp later conflicts nonlocally.
ideas.summary: Try to define a two-level resolved-surplus/debt recursion. A low-dominated drought creates surplus relative to old high history; assigning low quote mass reduces low regret but creates high debt at the next resolving high. Seek upper and lower bounds for D_n or fixed-envelope feasibility via a reflected-workload invariant.
ideas.title: Resolved-Surplus Debt Recursion
ideas.why_promising: It directly targets the current bottleneck: replacing the refuted raw Q_T localization by a state variable that remembers both surplus and future high debt.

ideas.risks: The augmented LP may become a tautological restatement of the global fixed-envelope criterion unless the shadow objectives are restricted in a useful way.
ideas.summary: Define a boundary-augmented prefix LP that retains late shadow thresholds/horizon weights when splitting a dual certificate. Use the exact boundary identity to ask whether repeated boundary defects either produce comparable-scale D_n mass or are discharged by measurable future quote opportunities.
ideas.title: Boundary-Augmented Localization
ideas.why_promising: It directly addresses the known failure of charging boundary defect to the shorter real prefix.

ideas.risks: Fresh quote opportunities after each low may always allow a path-aware policy to repair old conflicts; cumulative checks may make D_n linear after all.
ideas.summary: Search for an infinite market-path separator between D_n=o(n) and the fixed-envelope criterion using repeated diluted droughts, with L_i much larger than N_i but N_i arranged so low-horizon demands recur. Calibrate each block using the solver's local formula; if no separator appears, prove gluing for this restricted class.
ideas.title: Repeated Diluted-Drought Separator
ideas.why_promising: Simple separated blocks failed because one old conflict is diluted; repeated diluted conflicts are the next plausible negative construction.

ideas.risks: Branch observability and horizon-aware pseudo-regret can trivialize the construction; the transfer lemma requires exact same-prefix laws and probability-weighted accounting.
ideas.summary: Use rare branches carrying long multi-threshold or drought gadgets to formalize an essential-sup obstruction: beta or gamma remains large on rare histories, while expected regret contribution p_i N_i kappa_i is o(T). Compute the exact p_i,N_i,L_i conditions and state which learner quantifiers it refutes.
ideas.title: Rare-Branch Hardness Calibration
ideas.why_promising: It would cleanly separate uniform conditional tail failure from expected decision-relevant regret, strengthening the counterexample bank.

ideas.risks: Existing delayed-reward literature is mostly not this suffix-horizon full-information model; discontinuous threshold rewards and exogeneity assumptions must be mapped carefully.
ideas.summary: Explore adaptive truncation/skipping algorithms for the finite-grid reduction using outstanding-observation or priority-queue ideas from delayed online learning. Aim for regret bounds in terms of skipped payoff-weighted unresolved fills rather than a fixed H or raw beta tail.
ideas.title: Adaptive Skipping Sufficiency
ideas.why_promising: This is independent of the known-path gluing problem and may yield a cleaner positive theorem aligned with modern delayed-feedback terminology.
